notes.title: Transport games sale on Steam has begun!
notes.notes:
Our studio has projects of different genres and themes in its portfolio. But our largest and most highly rated games are dedicated to transport: buses, trains and airplanes. Today, Planes, Trains, and Automobiles Fest starts on Steam. We are participating with three main games:

[b]About buses: Bus World.[/b] This is not another bus driver simulation game, but a unique experience in which you will face natural and man-made disasters. Although for lovers of quiet trips and scheduled flights, the game will also be able to please, because it has a Free Mode!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1193090/Bus_World/

[b]About airplanes: Fly Corp.[/b] This minimalistic, but extremely addictive transport strategy has already managed to charm the hearts of players from all over the world. Hop in and try to create a successful transport network!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1372530/Fly_Corp/

[b]About trains: Metro Simulator 2.[/b] The game boasts detailed recreations of real Metro stations and tunnels, as well as a realistic train control system.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1787480/Metro_Simulator_2/

If you are already familiar with one of our games, we invite you to try out the others, because all of them have generous discounts.

So, the most noticeable change is the new part of Chornobyl map. We expanded the forest part to the South from the Red Forest and added swamps there. This is also the place where two new scenarios take place. One of them features the rainy weather which was introduced not long ago and became even better now. For those who like creating their own routes, we added a bunch of bus stops in the new area.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36189081/e58095049b983b649da202c3c7915d41698685aa.png[/img]

Recently we published a video showcasing the new first person camera physics. Now you can take a look at it yourself. It reacts to all kinds of movement of the bus, including bumps. By the way, this new camera behavior is optional and can be disabled in Settings. It should work fine with TrackIR as well.

There are more good news for those who like taking a ride in Free Mode as they can now change weather from the Garage. But you can still choose random weather in the dropdown list.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36189081/fe7cf6fa737e7ac131c0605fce0b4c78826cd459.png[/img]

We made a lot of work to increase the overall quality of the game: made it easier and more understandable to leave the garage with or without a route in Free Mode, improved performance in some places (especially in Rockfall scenario), and gauges on Soviet buses now wander around a bit, just like they do in real life.

As you can clearly see, we are still adding new content to the game without forgetting to improve its quality and add new features. We're not stopping here, so stay tuned for more news. We'll tell you more about the future updates soon.

Before, buttons of controllers were read from each controller separately, unlike axles. Because of that, axles’ values could be recognized incorrectly. Now the game can distinguish the axles of the first 4 connected controllers.

What to wait in the next updates?

The top priority now is to fix known bugs. Also, we already have a list of things we'd like to improve.

Also, we're working on two more buses for the game. You can expect them to arrive before 2023.

Number of scenarios will also grow. Even now, not all roads of Chernobyl map are used in scenarios. We have ideas for some new scenarios.

Map expansion is also planned, for example we'd like to see more forest roads in Chernobyl (including ones with unique biomes, such as swamps).

All these updates will be free for everyone who owns the game!

Also, we don't forget about various input methods. Now there is a problem with steering wheels. We are working on fixing it. The patch will arrive soon.

Finally, we're constantly working on optimizing the game. We understand that some of you may be disappointed by dynamic map loading in Chernobyl. We'll try to make these loads much less noticeable.

notes.title: Forced re-work of buses and traffic vehicles
notes.notes:
During this year, we've faced many challenges, and we have to make difficult decisions.

In this spring we received a complaint from one of the companies related to transport. They require us to pay a fine and remove content which is used illegally, in their opinion. We are still trying to insist that we aren't violating any copyrights, but it isn't a quick routine, and of course it takes money, time and mental health. It is still unknown what will happen in the end of this story.

In this regard, we took a decision that all vehicles in Bus World will look unlike any real ones to minimize the risk of receiving more complaints. That goes for both buses and traffic cars.

Buses will have their own names - we came up with a few fictional manufacturers. Of course, we consider the direction of design solutions during the years when the real bus was manufactured.

On the screenshots below you can see Soviet buses OSB-3101, OSB Vostok and a modern bus which you can drive in Southern China.

notes.title: We wish you merry Christmas and happy New Year!
notes.notes:
Our team wishes you merry Christmas and happy New Year!

2021 was an important year for both our team and bus simulators we've been working on all this time.

Bus Driver Simulator has received 15 updates during 2021, both small and big ones. For example, in the beginning of the year we released five unique and interesting scenarios for Murom Suburbs DLC: driving with potato bags in passenger compartment and creating New Year mood in the corresponding scenario. In Summer, we released the new map called Russian Soul, which was highly rated by players (its rating in Steam is now over 80%). The most noticeable update of this Fall is support for Steam Workshop with custom liveries. Finally, we released Bus Driver Simulator: Countryside on PS4 and Xbox One.

Another bus simulator Bus World has made even more progress. Despite the fact that it's in development for 2 and a half years, it began to look playable only this year. We finished many systems and components we've been working on since previous year and fully changed rendering pipeline to HDRP. We learned and implemented dozens of new methods and workarounds to improve performance, which was very bad just after we moved to HDRP. And, gameplay started to feel really nice when we added scenarios with unusual conditions such as tsunami or tornado.

Now we can easily state that Bus World is on the polishing stage. We're fixing bugs, making the balance better, finishing scenarios, adding various details and working on making performance even better. Of course, we've still got a lot to do, but our test builds are already playable, and the game is moving to its release version step by step.

Of course, we have huge plans for 2022: we're planning to release Bus World and provide it with updates for the whole year.

We wish you to take a good rest on these holidays and have only good events in 2022!

notes.title: A little about scenarios
notes.notes:
We are putting high hopes on Bus World.

For us, it's a new step and possibility to show you our ideas on how the game about public transport can have story. Even though these stories are not complex, every scenario is unique in its own way while telling its story about the life of a bus driver: saving people from tornado, evacuation from the city contaminated by radiation, driving people to firework festival.

With each new scenario, events and places change. Regular scenarios and terrifying events where you can save people are waiting for you. We think that such contrast make the game more immersive.

Topic of disasters, both natural and human-made, is not very common in videogames, and we're happy that we're the ones who can give a new breath to this genre by combining gameplay situations and bringing up different topics.

There are 17 scenarios in the game. They are now being improved, and we plan to make even more scenarios by the time the game is released.

notes.title: More screenshots: Duga Radar Station

You will be able to drive to military town Chernobyl-2 and Duga radar station. This is a station which was meant to early detect launches of intercontinental ballistic missiles. Its task was to detect missiles launched from USA by measuring the ionization of the ionosphere caused by gas from rocket engines. The antenna is huge: its height varies from 135 to 150m in different points, and its length is 300 to 500 meters. According to some sources, it's even more expensive than Chernobyl Power Plant itself. It's clear that it was built near the nuclear power plant due to its huge power consumption. The tragic thing about Duga-1 is that it was not even used: it was scheduled to be started in 1986, the year, when the Chernobyl disaster happened.

notes.title: The summary of 2020
notes.notes:
2020 has come to an end, and now it's time to conclude this year.
We'll begin from the start. In January 2020, we released a big and important update for Bus Driver Simulator, which allowed you to create your own routes. Some time after such an update is released, we are wondering how we could live without that feature before.
In a couple of months after that, one of the most popular city buses was released.
We still were supporting Bus Driver Simulator, but, after making sure that there are no critical bugs in the game, finally transferred our forces to Bus World.

We've done a lot while developing Bus World, which is an ambitious project, but we still got to do, at minimal, the same amount of work. When we finally finished with constantly updating our previous game, we finally were able to learn more about new technologies which will make our game better. One of them is High Definition Rendering Pipeline, which allows the lighting, materials and other things in the game to be a lot more realistic. Of course, transition to HDRP was not east - we needed at least a month to do that. However, it was worth it: volumetric fog, correct lighting behavior, no strange flickering and other artifacts, and graphics quality became much better.
We're glad to bring some new things to this genre: probably, there is no game about breakdowns and disasters like Bus World.
You constantly ask us when the game will be released, but we still got a lot of work to do, so we won't announce it now as we don't want to accidentally lie to you.

We made a lot inside our team. This organizational work is invisible for you, players, but it is very important to help us become more professional. We're still a small studio, but we're working on large games - and we have to constantly work on team management to make it possible. The main thing is that even now we can see the result of these changes.

And, of course, Murom Suburbs - we managed to launch the biggest DLC for Bus Driver Simulator ever in 2020. Even though we said that there won't be a lot of changes in the game, we implemented some things about traffic and navigation from Bus World, and we hope you liked them. The work on Bus World has been slightly slowed down due to the same people working on Bus Driver Simulator and Bus World. But, in the next year, after we finish with Murom Suburbs, we'll transfer our forces to Bus World again.

Finally, we express special thanks to our players. We know that most of you are with us for several years. Your support is crucial in this business. We will do our best to make sure you enjoy our future projects - we have a lot of plans!

Our team congratulates you with coming New 2021 Year!

notes.title: Transition to HDRP and release date postponed to 2021
notes.notes:
As we said before, we'd like to make Bus World better than any our games. In order to achieve this, the decision was made to move to the new renderer: HDRP. It was created specifically for ambitious projects with high level of detail. The difference between Built-In (the default Unity renderer which we used before) is noticeable: the picture looks much more "alive" thanks to the new renderer. Take a look at the screenshots which we took in Editor, without anti-aliasing: also, we'd be able to use volumetric lighting.
However, this is a big challenge for our team. It's not that easy to make it as we have to work with new tools and learn how to use them. It's about making night/day cycle, mirrors and plants from scratch. This requires quite a lot of time, and we don't want our game to be released in a buggy state, so we have to postpone the release date to 2021. We'll announce the more accurate release date when we're ready.

notes.title: Recreating Chernobyl for Bus World. Pripyat central square.
notes.notes:
In our new game, we have set ourselves a difficult, but very interesting task - to recreate the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone in its state in April, 1986. Probably, this wasn't done in any game before (excluding mods and games like Stalker, where locations are made like in the reality, but placement of objects is different).

As you can see, the map proportions are real. We are planning to recreate the central street of Pripyat and roads to Jupiter factory, Janov station, Red Forest, radiolocational station Duga, Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant and surroundings, the central street of Chernobyl etc.

But today we'll show you central street of Pripyat and compare it to the real one.

It’s quite hard to move a real city into a game. But it’s even harder to do it with the appearance of the city in the past. Pripyat, Chernobyl and other localities in Bus World will look very similar to their look just after the disaster in 1986.
In order to recreate this or that place, we have to look through a lot of photos and videos. Unfortunately, not all the needed materials can be found in the Internet. A suitable example is village of Kopachi, which was demolished because of extremely high radiation level. We have to rely on a very limited amount of video materials and fill in the blanks.
Chernobyl has been recreated in many games, but possibly, we're the first who are trying to recreate this zone according to the real location of all the buildings, roads and other objects. Thus, this is not only a game but a peculiar tour to Chernobyl as it was in 1986.
